vocabulary.systemTerm: Incident (incidents row; web 'Incident', mobile 'Case' for chiefs)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: One field report of a problem at a place on the state highway: District / County / Route / Post mile, a map pin, when it was first seen, description and photos.
vocabulary.why: Newcomers expect 'incident' to be the whole case; calling it a 'report' separates it from the Assessment work that follows. Use exactly this label everywhere (never 'Case', 'ticket' or 'field report'); the id shows as 'Incident #40' in muted text after the title, and the backend name 'Incident' stays in the tooltip and URL.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: One real-world event or site (a slide, a storm section) that several incident reports can belong to, so their history stays together.
vocabulary.why: Keep the backend word because staff already see it on the web, but attach this one-line definition the first time it appears on any screen (triage dialog, filters) via an inline info popover. Never say 'Project' on web; mobile and the cross-section save dialog must be flagged as a naming defect. Chips read 'Event Group · I-80 Emigrant Gap', id last in muted text.

vocabulary.uiLabel: Event Group (do not use 'Project' in UI)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Retired synonym for Event Group; reads to Caltrans staff as a capital construction project, which it is not.
vocabulary.why: Two names for the same object was the highest-risk confusion in the brief. Remove from web copy; where the mobile app still says Project, show 'Event Group (formerly Project)' for one release.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The canonical place record a coordinator links a report to, so repeat reports at the same spot share one history.
vocabulary.why: The coordinator's job word is 'site/location'. Show 'Link to an existing site' / 'This is a new site' as the two choices; tooltip: 'Location record (EXISTING or CREATE_NEW)'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The permanent reference number a report gets when a coordinator accepts it into ERIS; reports still waiting for intake do not have one yet.
vocabulary.why: 'Permanent key' is never explained in the UI today and a missing one reads like a bug. 'ERIS number' is what people will read over the phone. Show as 'ERIS no. 24-0417' next to the title; before intake show 'Not yet accepted — no ERIS number'. Tooltip keeps 'incident_key'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Awaiting intake tab (current_stage COORDINATOR_REVIEW, no incident_key)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Reports the district coordinator has not yet reviewed; they are not part of the permanent record until accepted.
vocabulary.why: 'Intake' is coordinator jargon that mobile never uses (mobile says 'Under Review'). Tab label 'New reports' with the count; helper line 'Not yet accepted into ERIS'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Reports a coordinator has accepted; each has an ERIS number and a workflow position.
vocabulary.why: Pairs with 'New reports' so the two tabs read as before/after one action instead of 'intake' vs 'records'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The coordinator's one decision on a new report: which site or Event Group it belongs to and what should happen next.
vocabulary.why: 'Triage' is understood by coordinators but not by chiefs or engineers who see it in history. Primary button 'Review report'; the recorded outcome is the 'Decision'. Tooltip: 'Triage'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: What happens to the report after review: send to GeoTech for assessment, close with no assessment, ask the reporter for more information, or link it to an existing report.
vocabulary.why: 'Disposition' is legal/administrative vocabulary; 'Decision' matches the button 'Record decision'. Each option is a radio with a consequence sentence; the enum value stays in the tooltip and the history detail.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Accept the report, give it an ERIS number and open an Assessment for the GeoTech office that serves this district.
vocabulary.why: Names the consequence (who receives it) rather than the abstract state.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Accept the report for the record and close it; GeoTech is not involved.
vocabulary.why: Coordinators today choose 'Assessment required' by default because 'accept' and 'route' are conflated; this label makes clear the report is kept and closed.

vocabulary.uiLabel: Ask the reporter for more information
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Send the report back to the person who filed it, naming the fields to fix; it returns to your queue when they resubmit.
vocabulary.why: Distinguishes the reporter loop from the engineer's 'Returned for changes' loop, which the brief found people confuse.

vocabulary.uiLabel: Link to an existing report and close
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: This report describes something already in ERIS; keep it, link it to that report or site, and close it. Nothing is deleted.
vocabulary.why: Users think 'duplicate' means the report is thrown away; the label and helper say it is kept and linked.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The GeoTech work opened for an accepted report: who it is handed to, the engineer's technical form, review and sign-off.
vocabulary.why: Keep the official product word; the fix is to stop showing three ids. Header pattern: incident title first, then 'Assessment for ERIS no. 24-0417 · Route 1 PM 12.3 · Los Angeles'. The mobile form step literally named 'Assessment' must be renamed 'Findings' (flag as mobile change).

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The engineer's detailed geotechnical write-up for one assessment (the form Caltrans staff know as the GISA): site, measurements, findings, photos, recommendations.
vocabulary.why: 'Submission' reads as the act of sending; 'GISA' is banned on web by docs but staff know it. Use 'Technical form' as the label and put 'GISA · Submission #9' in the tooltip/eyebrow so veterans can map it. One name across My Work, Assessments, the form page and mobile Drafts/Submissions tabs.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Submission status DRAFT / SUBMITTED / APPROVED / REJECTED
vocabulary.uiLabel: Form status: Draft / Sent for review / Approved / Returned for changes
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Where the technical form itself is; it should always agree with the Assessment stage.
vocabulary.why: 'REJECTED' reads as final rejection; the job word is 'returned'. Today the form and the assessment can disagree (form SUBMITTED while assessment REVISION_REQUESTED) — flag as a backend change: keep both machines in sync on review actions.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Draft (assessment DRAFT / submission DRAFT / mobile local draft)
vocabulary.uiLabel: Draft (form not yet sent) / 'Saved on this device' (mobile offline draft)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Work the engineer has started but not sent for review; an offline draft exists only on the device until it syncs.
vocabulary.why: Three different 'drafts' exist. Show 'Draft' only for the technical form, and label device-only copies 'Saved on this device — not yet synced'.

vocabulary.uiLabel: Hand off to a branch chief
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The office chief chooses which branch chief takes this assessment, and may name the engineer at the same time.
vocabulary.why: 'Delegate' is fine for chiefs but 'hand off to' states the receiver. Form labels: 'Branch chief' (required) and 'Engineer (optional — skips the branch chief step)'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The branch chief names the engineer who will visit the site and write the technical form.
vocabulary.why: Already plain. Picker options must show name, branch and open-assessment count instead of 'name · email'; never a raw user id.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Assignment roles ENGINEER / REVIEWER / APPROVER / CONSULTED (assessment_assignments)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: People attached to one assessment: the engineer does the work, reviewers and approvers can approve or return it, consulted people only receive it for information.
vocabulary.why: Only Reviewer/Approver can act; 'Consulted (no approval authority)' must say so inline because the legacy REVIEWER job role also exists and grants nothing.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: An assigned reviewer reads the technical form and either approves it or returns it to the engineer with comments.
vocabulary.why: Today the same action is 'Request revision', 'Return for correction' and 'Reject' in three places. One pair of verbs: 'Approve' and 'Return for changes' (comment required).

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The office chief's final acceptance of an approved assessment; it locks the assessment but does not close the incident report.
vocabulary.why: Users assume Finalized = case closed. Confirmation copy must say 'The incident report stays open until it is marked resolved.' Tooltip: 'Finalize'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Resolve (POST /incidents/{id}/resolve; also the result of NO_ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED and DUPLICATE_OR_LINKED)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Close the incident report itself; the reason (assessment signed off, no assessment needed, linked to another report) is shown with it.
vocabulary.why: 'Resolved' currently hides why. Always pair the label with the reason line so a report closed at review is distinguishable from one closed after an assessment.

vocabulary.systemTerm: incident.status NEW / IN_PROGRESS / RESOLVED vs current_stage vs assessment state
vocabulary.uiLabel: One 'Where is it' line per report
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: A single plain sentence that combines the three backend machines: who has the report right now and what they are doing with it.
vocabulary.why: Three parallel vocabularies (status, stage, state) are the brief's 'very high' risk. The UI shows one status chip + one owner sentence derived from all three; the raw codes live in a 'Technical details' disclosure.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Everything waiting on you, grouped by the action you need to take.
vocabulary.why: Keep the name; fix the framing: section headers 'To review (3)', 'To hand off (2)', 'To sign off (1)', 'Returned to you (1)' and 'Waiting on you' instead of 'Waiting on Office Chief'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The statewide map of Event Groups, their incident reports and field photos.
vocabulary.why: 'Mission Center' sounds like a dispatch console and coordinators looked for 'Map'. Nav label 'Map'; page eyebrow 'Mission Center' keeps the internal name for docs and deep links.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Terrain Cross Section (GIS Tools > Terrain Cross Sections; DEM profile, aerial capture)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Draw a line on the 3D terrain to get an elevation profile and an aerial snapshot of the ground along it.
vocabulary.why: Distinguishes it from the roadway cross-section diagram inside the technical form ('Roadway section') and from the 3D terrain viewer. Tooltip: 'Terrain cross section (DEM profile)'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Measurements / roadway cross-section diagram (GISA measurements, Failure side LT/RT)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The engineer's sketch of the road cross-section with distances, lane widths and which side failed (left or right facing increasing post mile).
vocabulary.why: Avoids collision with 'Terrain profile'. Spell out 'LT (left)' / 'RT (right)' on first use in each session.

vocabulary.systemTerm: 3D Terrain scene (SceneView in the form's Measurements card)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: An interactive 3D view of the ground around the site; loads only on request and only on devices that support it.
vocabulary.why: Separates viewing (this) from drawing (Terrain profile). Button 'Load 3D terrain' with a static preview so phones and low-memory iPads are not blocked.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Caltrans' distance marker along a route within a county, e.g. PM 12.30.
vocabulary.why: Known to every Caltrans employee; keep it, always with the 'PM' prefix and two decimals, never 'PM ?'. First-use tooltip for outsiders.

vocabulary.uiLabel: Location: District · County · Route · Post mile
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The Caltrans way of naming a place on the highway, e.g. 'District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 1 · PM 12.30'.
vocabulary.why: Expand the abbreviations in labels ('D07', 'LA', 'R001' become 'District 7', 'Los Angeles', 'Route 1'); one shared helper produces this string for rails, cards and headers so 'Route' never collides with office routing.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Routing / office_code NORTH / SOUTH / WEST / routing override
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Which Geotechnical Services office (North, South or West) serves the report's district; coordinators can choose a different office with a reason.
vocabulary.why: 'Routing' collides with highway 'Route'. Say 'GeoTech office: North (based on District 3)' and 'Send to a different office' for the override; show office names, never codes.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Admin table of which coordinator receives each district's new reports and which chiefs belong to each GeoTech office.
vocabulary.why: Third meaning of 'routing'; naming it by its question avoids the collision. A district with nobody listed shows a warning 'New reports here have no coordinator'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Road Inventory / RI context / dataset version / authoritative version / mobile package
vocabulary.uiLabel: Road Inventory (published version, offline copy for the app)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Caltrans' roadway reference data (lanes, surface, segments) that ERIS matches each report to; admins publish new versions and generate the offline copy the mobile app downloads.
vocabulary.why: 'Authoritative', 'manifest', 'superseded' and 'mobile package' are undefined today. Use 'Published version', 'Previous versions', 'Offline copy for the app'; on the reporter's list say 'Matched to Road Inventory' instead of 'RI context saved · Dataset X · Seg Y'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Workflow tree / current owner (nodes REPORTER_SUBMISSION ... RESOLUTION; UNASSIGNED)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The step-by-step trail of a report from filing to resolution, showing who holds it now.
vocabulary.why: 'Workflow tree' is developer vocabulary. 'UNASSIGNED' must read 'Waiting for someone to be assigned' rather than looking like an error.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Every photo, video and document attached to a technical form, with where and in which direction each photo was taken.
vocabulary.why: Three names for one thing. 'Photos and files' is the section; 'Mapped photos' is the filter that shows telemetry. Tooltip keeps 'Submission library'.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: The small wedge on the map showing which way the camera was pointing.
vocabulary.why: Legend entry text; 'heading' alone is aviation/GIS vocabulary.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Changes saved on this device that will be sent when the connection returns; if one fails, the ones behind it wait too.
vocabulary.why: Reporters need to know a report is not yet in ERIS. Show count and 'Retry' rather than 'queue'.

vocabulary.systemTerm: Field worker (legacy code FIELD_WORKER = GeoTech engineer) vs Maintenance field worker (reporter)
vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Two different people: the engineer who assesses (legacy code FIELD_WORKER) and the maintenance crew member who files reports (MAINTENANCE / MAINTENANCE_FIELD_WORKER).
vocabulary.why: The plain-English meaning of the code is the opposite of its role. Never print role codes; the roles table below is the only source of labels.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Internal term for roles that can see all reports and assessments; it should never appear in copy.
vocabulary.why: Gates nav visibility only; if a denied user hits a gated URL the message names the page, not the gate ('You do not have access to Event Groups').

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: List of every technical form, useful for engineers and reviewers looking up an older write-up.
vocabulary.why: Reachable by URL with older vocabulary; either give it this nav label under Operations or fold it into Assessments. It must stop being the fallback redirect for denied users.

vocabulary.oneLineDefinition: Retired self-assignment endpoint that now returns an error.
vocabulary.why: Also rename the 'Unclaimed only' filter to 'Unassigned only'.

statuses.label: New
statuses.meaning: Report filed; nobody has accepted it yet. Note: today NEW also persists after acceptance while current_stage moves on — the UI must derive the chip from stage + location_match_status, not from status alone.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Coordinator: 'Review this report — decide where it belongs and what happens next.' Reporter: 'Your report is with the District {n} coordinator for review.'

statuses.label: In progress
statuses.meaning: Accepted and being worked by GeoTech; the stage line says by whom.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Show the stage sentence instead of this word: e.g. 'With North GeoTech Office — waiting for hand-off to a branch chief.'

statuses.label: Resolved
statuses.meaning: The report is closed. Always shown with its reason: assessment signed off, no assessment needed, or linked to another report.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Resolved {date} by {name} — {reason}.' No action button.

statuses.label: Waiting for coordinator review
statuses.meaning: Not yet accepted into ERIS; no ERIS number.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Coordinator: 'Review report.' Others: 'The District {n} coordinator has not reviewed this report yet.'

statuses.label: Waiting on reporter
statuses.meaning: The coordinator asked the reporter to fix specific fields; review resumes when they resubmit.
statuses.whoActsNext: The person who filed the report
statuses.nextStepCopy: Reporter: 'The coordinator needs more information: {fields}. Update your report to send it back.' Coordinator: 'Waiting for {reporter name} to update {fields} — sent {date}.' (Do not offer 'Review report' here.)

statuses.label: Location not yet confirmed
statuses.meaning: The coordinator has not yet confirmed the site / Event Group.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Shown only inside the review dialog: 'Confirm the site this report belongs to.'

statuses.label: With GeoTech office — awaiting hand-off
statuses.meaning: Accepted; the GeoTech office chief has not yet handed the assessment to a branch chief.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Office chief: 'Hand this assessment off to a branch chief.' Coordinator/reporter: 'Accepted and sent to the {office} GeoTech Office on {date}.'

statuses.label: With branch chief — awaiting engineer
statuses.meaning: A branch chief has it and must name the engineer.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Branch chief: 'Assign an engineer to visit the site.' Others: 'Handed off to {branch chief name} on {date}; an engineer has not been assigned yet.'

statuses.label: Engineer assigned — {engineer name}
statuses.meaning: An engineer owns the site work; the assessment state says whether the form is in draft, under review, returned, approved or signed off.
statuses.whoActsNext: The named engineer (or reviewer / office chief per assessment state)
statuses.nextStepCopy: Use the assessment-state sentence below; the incident line reads 'Engineer {name} assigned {date}.'

statuses.label: Resolved
statuses.meaning: Terminal stage; same as status RESOLVED.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Resolved {date} — {reason}.'

statuses.label: Sent to GeoTech for assessment
statuses.meaning: Coordinator accepted the report and opened an Assessment.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Confirmation: 'Report accepted as ERIS no. {key} and sent to the {office} GeoTech Office. It has left your queue.'

statuses.label: Closed — no assessment needed
statuses.meaning: Kept for the record and closed at review.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Confirmation: 'Report accepted and closed. No GeoTech assessment will be opened.'

statuses.label: Waiting on reporter
statuses.meaning: Sent back for specific fields; stays in the coordinator's district but in a separate 'Waiting on reporter' section.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Confirmation: 'Sent back to {reporter}. You will see it under Waiting on reporter until they update {fields}.'

statuses.label: Linked to another report — closed
statuses.meaning: Closed and linked to an existing report or site; nothing deleted.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Confirmation: 'Linked to ERIS no. {target} and closed. Both reports keep their photos and history.'

statuses.label: Awaiting hand-off to branch chief
statuses.meaning: Opened by the coordinator's decision; the office chief must choose a branch chief (optionally naming the engineer).
statuses.nextStepCopy: Office chief: 'Hand off to a branch chief. You can name the engineer now to skip the branch step.' Others: 'Waiting for the {office} office chief to hand this off.'

statuses.label: Awaiting engineer assignment
statuses.meaning: A branch chief holds it and must name the engineer; reviewers can be added at the same time.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Branch chief: 'Assign an engineer. Handed to you by {office chief} on {date}{: note}.' Others: 'Waiting for {branch chief} to assign an engineer.'

statuses.label: Engineer working — draft
statuses.meaning: The assigned engineer is completing the technical form; nothing has been sent for review.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Engineer: 'Complete the technical form, then send it for review.' (Button 'Send for review' disabled with reason 'Add at least one technical form first' when none exists.) Others: '{engineer} is preparing the technical form.'

statuses.label: Under review
statuses.meaning: The engineer sent the form; an assigned reviewer or approver must approve it or return it. If no reviewer is assigned, review is blocked.
statuses.whoActsNext: Assigned reviewer / approver (or a chief must assign one)
statuses.nextStepCopy: Reviewer: 'Read the technical form, then Approve or Return for changes.' Chief when no reviewer exists: 'Review is blocked — assign a reviewer.' Engineer: 'Sent for review {date}. Waiting for {reviewer names}.'

statuses.label: Returned for changes
statuses.meaning: A reviewer sent it back; the engineer must revise and resend. The reviewer's comment is the most important thing on the screen.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Engineer: 'Returned by {reviewer} on {date}: "{comment}". Update the technical form and send it again.' Reviewer: 'Waiting for {engineer} to make the changes you asked for.'

statuses.label: Approved — awaiting sign-off
statuses.meaning: Review passed; the office chief must sign off to lock the assessment.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Office chief: 'Sign off this assessment. The incident report stays open until it is marked resolved.' Others: 'Approved by {reviewer} on {date}; waiting for the office chief's sign-off.'

statuses.label: Signed off
statuses.meaning: The assessment is complete and locked. The incident report may still be open.
statuses.whoActsNext: Assigned engineer or admin, to resolve the incident report
statuses.nextStepCopy: Engineer: 'Assessment signed off {date}. Mark the incident report resolved when the site work is done.' Others: 'Signed off {date} by {office chief}.'

statuses.label: Draft
statuses.meaning: Being written; editable by the assigned engineer.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Draft saved {time}. Send for review when every required section is complete ({n} of {m} done).'

statuses.label: Sent for review
statuses.meaning: Locked for editing while reviewers read it.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Reviewer: 'Approve or Return for changes (comment required).' Engineer: 'Read-only while under review.'

statuses.label: Returned for changes
statuses.meaning: Sent back with comments; editable again. Never show the word 'Rejected'.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Returned by {reviewer} {date}: "{comment}". Edit and send again.' (Backend flag: keep assessment REVISION_REQUESTED in sync so this item appears in the engineer's My Work.)

statuses.label: Approved
statuses.meaning: Review passed; read-only.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Approved {date} by {reviewer}.'

statuses.label: Open
statuses.meaning: Active site/event; new reports can be linked to it.
statuses.nextStepCopy: '{n} open reports · last activity {date}.'

statuses.label: Closed
statuses.meaning: No active reports; can be reopened by a coordinator.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Closed {date} by {name}. Reopen if new reports arrive at this site.'

statuses.label: Archived
statuses.meaning: Legacy group kept for history only; cannot be reopened.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Archived — history only.'

statuses.label: Done
statuses.meaning: Step finished, with actor and date.
statuses.nextStepCopy: '{step} — {name}, {date}.'

statuses.label: Now
statuses.meaning: The active step and its owner.
statuses.nextStepCopy: '{step} — with {name}' (or 'with you').

statuses.label: Not yet
statuses.meaning: A later step that cannot start yet.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Rendered muted with no sentence.

statuses.label: Waiting on reporter
statuses.meaning: Paused until the reporter updates the report.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Waiting for {reporter} to update {fields}.'

statuses.label: Returned for changes
statuses.meaning: Engineering step reopened after review.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Returned to {engineer} by {reviewer}, {date}.'

statuses.label: Needs someone assigned
statuses.meaning: The step is active but no person holds it (e.g. no district coordinator, no reviewer).
statuses.whoActsNext: The chief or admin who can assign
statuses.nextStepCopy: Chief/admin: 'Nobody is assigned to {step} — assign a {role}.' Others: 'Waiting for a {role} to be assigned.'

statuses.label: Not needed
statuses.meaning: Step bypassed because the report was closed at review.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Not needed — closed at coordinator review.'

statuses.label: Resolved
statuses.meaning: Final step reached.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Resolved {date} — {reason}.'

statuses.label: Imported — not yet published
statuses.meaning: Uploaded and checked; ERIS is not using it yet.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Publish version {tag} to make it the one ERIS uses.'

statuses.label: Published (in use)
statuses.meaning: The version ERIS matches reports against.
statuses.whoActsNext: Admin (regenerate offline copy if not done)
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Published {date}. Offline copy for the app: {Ready {date} | Not generated — Generate now}.'

statuses.label: Previous version
statuses.meaning: Replaced by a newer published version; can be restored.
statuses.nextStepCopy: 'Restore this version' (destructive styling, confirmation names the version it replaces).

statuses.label: Waiting to start / Importing… / Imported / Failed
statuses.meaning: Progress of an Excel upload; the raw 'stage' string is hidden.
statuses.nextStepCopy: Imported: '{rows} rows imported, {skipped} skipped. Publish version {tag}.' Failed: '{error}. Fix the file and import again.'

statuses.label: Waiting to upload / Upload failed
statuses.meaning: Saved on the device; not yet in ERIS.
statuses.nextStepCopy: '{n} items waiting to upload — they will send when you are back online.' Failed: 'Upload stopped at {item}. Retry.'

roles.label: GeoTech Engineer (legacy code — not the maintenance reporter)
Reviewer (legacy account role — grants no review authority; review rights come from being assigned to an assessment)
Coordinator / Office chief / Branch chief / Engineer on this report

emptyStates.screen: My Work — Maintenance Coordinator, 'Needs my decision' section empty
emptyStates.copy: No new reports to review. Field reports for District {n} appear here the moment they are filed from the mobile app.
emptyStates.action: See accepted reports (→ Incidents, Accepted tab) · Secondary: 'Waiting on reporter ({n})' section stays visible when non-empty

emptyStates.screen: My Work — Maintenance Coordinator, 'Waiting on reporter' section empty
emptyStates.copy: Nothing is waiting on a reporter.

emptyStates.screen: My Work — GeoTech Office Chief, 'To hand off' empty
emptyStates.copy: No assessments are waiting for hand-off. New ones arrive when a coordinator sends a report to the {office} office.
emptyStates.action: View all {office} assessments (→ Assessments filtered to my office, active only)

emptyStates.screen: My Work — GeoTech Office Chief, 'To sign off' empty
emptyStates.copy: Nothing to sign off. Approved assessments from your office appear here.
emptyStates.action: View assessments under review (→ Assessments, state Under review, my office)

emptyStates.screen: My Work — GeoTech Branch Chief, 'To assign' empty
emptyStates.copy: No assessments are waiting for an engineer. Your office chief hands assessments to you here.
emptyStates.action: See my branch's active assessments (→ Assessments filtered to my branch)

emptyStates.screen: My Work — GeoTech Engineer, 'My assessments' empty
emptyStates.copy: You have no assessments right now. A branch chief assigns them to you after a report is accepted; you will be notified.
emptyStates.action: Open Terrain profile tool · Browse accepted reports (→ Incidents)

emptyStates.screen: My Work — GeoTech Engineer, 'Returned to you' empty
emptyStates.copy: Nothing has been returned for changes.

emptyStates.screen: My Work — Reviewer / Approver, 'To review' empty
emptyStates.copy: Nothing is waiting for your review. Technical forms appear here when an engineer sends one on an assessment you are assigned to.
emptyStates.action: See assessments I am assigned to (→ Assessments filtered 'Assigned to me')

emptyStates.screen: My Work — Administrator (default 'Assigned to me' filter) empty
emptyStates.copy: Nothing is assigned to you. Switch to 'Everything' to see every step waiting anywhere in ERIS, including districts with no coordinator.
emptyStates.action: Show everything · Check who covers each district (→ Administration)

emptyStates.screen: My Work — any role, filter chips narrow to zero
emptyStates.copy: No items match '{filter}'. {n} other items are waiting on you.

emptyStates.screen: Incidents — 'New reports' tab empty
emptyStates.copy: No new reports are waiting for review in {district scope}. New field reports show here until a coordinator accepts them.
emptyStates.action: Show accepted reports · File a report (roles with canReportIncident only)

emptyStates.screen: Incidents — 'Accepted reports' tab empty (no filters)
emptyStates.copy: No accepted reports yet. Reports appear here after a coordinator reviews them; {n} are still under 'New reports'.

emptyStates.screen: Incidents — search/filter returns nothing
emptyStates.copy: No reports match '{query}' in {tab}. Try the other tab or widen the district and status filters.
emptyStates.action: Search all reports (both tabs, all districts) · Clear filters

emptyStates.screen: Incidents — Maintenance Field Reporter's own reports (web)
emptyStates.copy: You have not filed any reports from this account. Reports are normally filed from the ERIS mobile app; you can also file one here.

emptyStates.screen: Event Groups list — no groups in scope
emptyStates.copy: No open Event Groups. A coordinator creates one when the first report at a new site is accepted.

emptyStates.screen: Event Groups list — search returns nothing
emptyStates.copy: No open Event Groups match '{query}'. It may be closed or archived.
emptyStates.action: Search all Event Groups (sets status to All)

emptyStates.screen: Event Group detail — no incidents

onboarding: Do NOT build a welcome tour, coach-mark carousel or video (NN/g: skipped, not remembered, no performance gain; staff rotate and touch ERIS only during events). Onboarding budget goes into the four items below.

First-run (once per account, dismissible, recallable): on the first visit to My Work show a single inline card above the queue titled 'How your work flows' for the signed-in role: 3–5 steps in plain status vocabulary with the user's step highlighted (Coordinator: Report filed → You review → GeoTech assesses → Signed off → Resolved; Office chief: Report accepted → You hand off → Branch chief assigns → Engineer writes → Review → You sign off; Branch chief; Engineer; Reviewer; Admin gets 'Where things get stuck' instead). One line per step, one sentence on what leaves your queue and where it goes. Closes with 'Got it' and is always re-openable from the Help panel.

Role-specific 'How work flows' panel, permanent: the same content lives in the Help panel (same header slot on every page, WCAG 3.2.6) with a second tab 'Words used in ERIS' (the vocabulary table above, filtered to terms visible on the current page first) and a third 'Contact GeoTech support'. The panel is a side sheet on desktop/iPad landscape and a bottom sheet on phones; it never covers the primary action bar.

Empty states carry the teaching: every queue and list uses the copy above (why it is empty, what will appear, one action). This replaces onboarding prose repeated on every item (e.g. the triage explanatory paragraph and the 'Read-only record view' banner become a one-time hint).

Just-in-time definitions instead of a glossary tour: the first time a session shows 'Event Group', 'ERIS number', 'Sign off', 'Returned for changes' or 'GeoTech office', render the term with a dotted underline and a tap/click info popover containing the one-line definition; after the popover is opened once the underline stays but the auto-hint does not repeat. Never hover-only (iPad).

Coach marks: only two, each a single anchored callout with a dismiss button, shown once per account: (a) on the coordinator's first review dialog, pointing at the Event Group radio list: 'Pick the site this report belongs to — nothing is saved until you press Record decision'; (b) on the engineer's first technical form, pointing at the section list: 'Sections can be completed in any order; your work autosaves.' Nothing else earns a coach mark.

Success confirmations as onboarding: after every workflow action (accept, hand off, assign, send for review, approve, return, sign off, resolve) show a persistent notice that names the object, the new state and where it went ('Assessment for ERIS no. 24-0417 handed off to Maria Chen. It has left your queue and is now under Assessments.') with an 'Undo' where the backend allows and an 'Open it' link. Users learn the flow by doing it.

Consequence-stating confirmations for irreversible steps (Close — no assessment, Link and close, Approve, Return for changes, Sign off, Resolve, Disable user, Publish/Restore Road Inventory): one sentence of consequence, the note/comment field inside the dialog, Cancel receives initial focus, the primary is disabled only while submitting (never silently).

Rotating-staff return path: when an account has not signed in for 60+ days, re-show the 'How your work flows' card once. Keep 'Recently done by me (7 days)' collapsed sections in My Work so people can see where their last actions went.

Role labels are onboarding: the header shows one humanized primary role ('GeoTech Branch Chief'); the avatar menu lists all roles with one-line descriptions; the Users admin page shows the same descriptions next to each role chip so admins provision correctly (and shows canonical names only, legacy aliases in tooltip).
contextualHelp: Rule 1 — Nothing essential lives in a tooltip. Units, required markers, formats, what photo to take and why a button is disabled are visible text under the label or next to the control. Tooltips (title attributes) are only for the backend name of a term staff already know ('Finalize', 'incident_key', 'GISA', 'Triage') and for icon-only buttons, which must also have aria-label.

Rule 2 — Every disabled primary action shows its reason inline in the same sentence position, e.g. 'Send for review — add at least one technical form first', 'Hand off — choose a branch chief first', 'Record decision — pick a site or choose New site'. Never a disabled button with a hover-only explanation.

Rule 3 — Every workflow object has one Next-step card at the top: status chip + 'Waiting on you' or 'Waiting on {name} ({role})' + one sentence from the status table + one primary button (secondary actions in a menu). The reviewer's comment, when present, is quoted inside this card, attributed by name and date.

Rule 4 — Definitions on first use: terms in the vocabulary table render with an info affordance (visible 'i' button or dotted underline that opens on tap/click and on Enter/Space) the first time they appear on a page; the popover has the one-line definition and a 'More in Help' link. No hover-only reveal.

Rule 5 — Consistent help slot: a 'Help' button in the same header position on every page opens the Help panel (How your work flows / Words used in ERIS / Contact support). Deep links: help panel opens to the section for the current page. WCAG 3.2.6.

Rule 6 — Forms: each field has label + visible hint (unit as a suffix outside the input, example value) + on-blur format validation for typed measurements only; completeness checks run on 'Mark section complete' and 'Send for review' with an error summary at the top that links to each field and moves focus there. Errors are fix-oriented ('Enter the post mile as a number, e.g. 12.40'), never 'invalid'. Entered text and photos are never cleared on error.

Rule 7 — Success and failure are stated where the user is looking: errors inside the open dialog (not behind the overlay), success notices anchored to the top of the panel that changed, and a toast on phones (bottom) with the same text. Every notice names the object.

Rule 8 — Status is never expressed by color alone: chip = fixed light background + dark text + short label (+ optional icon); map markers = shape + label; pipeline current step = label text 'Now' + aria-current='step'.

Rule 9 — Autosave and dirty state are visible: a status chip in the form header cycles 'Saving…' / 'Saved 14:32' / 'Offline — saved on this device' / 'Could not save — Retry', announced via aria-live=polite; explicit Save remains; leaving with unsaved changes asks first.

Rule 10 — Explanatory banners are shown once then collapse: 'Read-only record view — actions live in My Work' and the triage explanation become a dismissible one-line hint with an info icon that reopens it; dismissal is remembered per account.

Rule 11 — Codes are demoted, not deleted: a 'Technical details' disclosure on each record shows raw ids and enum values (incident id, assessment id, submission id, current_stage, state, office_code) for support calls; nothing else on the page prints an enum.

Rule 12 — Backend vocabulary appears exactly once per surface as a parenthetical or tooltip for the transition period ('Sign off (Finalize)'), removed after one release once training material catches up.
accessibilityChecklist: Target size (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 AA, ERIS policy): every interactive element ≥ 24×24 CSS px with 8 px spacing everywhere, and ≥ 44×44 px under @media (pointer: coarse) — includes rail cards, table row actions, filter chips, role chips, attachment tile buttons, map toolbar (ArcGIS view.ui widgets sized via CSS), 3D scene controls, pipeline steps, the ×/close of dialogs and the 'Remove file' buttons. Current 22–32 px controls fail.

Contrast, light theme (SC 1.4.3 / 1.4.11): text in --brand #1f9bd1, --good #1d9d5d and --bad #d14b54 on white or panel-soft is roughly 3.0–4.0:1 and FAILS 4.5:1 for the 11–13 px badge text and for white text on .btn-brand. Add per-theme text tokens (--brand-text, --good-text, --bad-text, --warn-text) for light: e.g. --brand-ink #0e4c6a for brand text, ≥ #157a47 for good, ≥ #b0303a for bad; keep the light hues for 3:1 borders/icons only. Verify every badge, link and button text ≥ 4.5:1 (no rounding) in all three themes with a build-time check.

Contrast, dark theme: --muted #a6badf on --panel #0f1d33 and --brand #4f9cff on panel pass; verify --line #233a61 borders on --panel reach 3:1 for form-field boundaries (SC 1.4.11) — likely fails; add a --line-strong token for input borders and focus rings.

Contrast, coastal theme: --brand #007b83, --good #137a57, --bad #b6454d on --panel #f9fcfb pass 4.5:1; check white-on-brand buttons (~5:1 ok) and the 12 px muted text --muted #4f7280 on --panel-soft #ecf6f4 (~4.6:1, borderline — do not use below 12 px).

Minimum text size: no UI text below 12 px (currently 74 tiny text nodes on the form page, 11 px chips throughout); body 14–16 px, table cells ≥ 13 px, and everything must reflow at 200% zoom without clipping.

Status not by color alone (SC 1.4.1): every status chip carries a text label and the same label appears in list rows; map markers encode status/priority by shape + label + a legend listing only visible operational symbols; the pipeline current step has aria-current='step' and the word 'Now'; unread/dirty/‘corrected’ pills include text.

Focus visible (SC 2.4.7, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured AA): a 2 px --brand ring on every control, rail card and link; sticky headers/action bars must not cover the focused element (use scroll-margin-top equal to header height; no fixed max-height nested scrollers that hide focus).

Keyboard path for every map (SC 2.1.1): every map view has a same-page equivalent list/table with the same records and filters; row selection highlights the marker and vice versa; ArcGIS MapView keyboard navigation (arrow pan, +/- zoom) is kept, the container has tabIndex=0 and an aria-label ('Map of Event Groups in California; use the list to select one'); popups open with an explicit 'Open' button; no action is marker-only.

Keyboard path for canvas/3D (SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2): the terrain-profile SVG chart is focusable with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (+Shift ×10) stepping and tap-to-pin; control points are editable from a list (Remove / Zoom to) so placing points by click is not the only way (coordinates can be typed); the SceneView is progressive enhancement with the elevation table and 2D map as the equivalent; no keyboard trap inside ArcGIS widgets (Escape returns focus to the toolbar).

Pointer gestures / dragging (SC 2.5.1, 2.5.7 AA): remove mouse-only drag/resize on the technical form; any remaining drag (sketch geometry, control points) has a single-pointer and keyboard alternative (typed coordinates, list reorder buttons). Pinch/pan on the map inside a scrolling page must not trap scrolling on touch — cap map height and require a tap to activate on phones.

Reflow (SC 1.4.10): at 320 px width and 400% zoom, headers, filters, form fields, dialogs and the Next-step card never scroll horizontally; only whole data tables and maps may (inside overflow-x-auto containers with tabIndex=0, a visible cut-off and aria-label). Replace the 520 px fixed canvas cards with a fluid grid.

Reduced motion (SC 2.3.3): honor prefers-reduced-motion for map goTo animations (use view.goTo(target, {animate:false})), marker flash/highlight (use static highlight), drawer/sheet slide-ins, skeleton shimmer and the 3D scene camera fly-to.

Live regions: one polite live region for autosave status ('Saving…', 'Saved 14:32', 'Offline — saved on this device'), queue reloads ('3 items waiting on you') and success notices; role='alert' for errors and for 'Could not save'; aria-busy on panels while a record loads; never announce on every keystroke.

Names and roles: every input/select/search has a programmatic label (aria-label or <label htmlFor>); icon buttons have aria-label; tab strips use role=tablist/tab/aria-selected; tables have <caption> and aria-sort on sortable headers; dialogs use role=dialog + aria-modal + aria-labelledby/-describedby, focus trap, Escape, focus return (the existing ModalDialog does this — the Save cross-section and Aerial capture dialogs must adopt it).

Page identity and navigation: document.title per route ('Assessment · ERIS no. 24-0417 — ERIS'); a skip-to-content link; the sidebar/drawer nav uses aria-current='page'; a breadcrumb on record pages; consistent Help location on every page (SC 3.2.6).

Forms (SC 3.3.1–3.3.3, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry AA): inline error text tied via aria-describedby and aria-invalid; error summary with links on submit; the technical form is prefilled from the incident (D/C/R/PM, coordinates, dates) so nothing already entered is re-typed; tri-state Yes/No/Unknown radios start unselected and are stacked on narrow screens.

Session and timeouts (SC 2.2.1, 2.2.5): warn before expiry, preserve the current URL and unsaved draft across re-authentication, and never discard a form on a network error (keep token on 5xx; retry UI).

Touch-only and hover-only: no hover-only affordances (tile actions, chip tooltips, hover-only link color); links are underlined; all title-attribute content is duplicated visibly or in the Technical details disclosure.

Media and images: photo thumbnails have alt text from caption/section ('Photo 3 — slope face, looking north'); video and PDF viewers have a visible fallback ('Open in new tab') on iOS where inline preview fails; map legends are real text, not images.

Testing gate for Caltrans/Section 508 review: automated axe run on every route in all three themes at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440 px and at 200%/400% zoom; manual keyboard walkthrough of the four core paths (coordinator review, hand-off/assign, engineer form send, reviewer approve) on desktop and iPad with VoiceOver; contrast report generated from the token file so theme changes cannot regress silently.
